calls.head: Something has to give
calls.body: The Capitals are one of the league’s best for chance quality, but the Kraken are near the top at preventing dangerous shots. Our lean: the Capitals’ chance quality wins out.

calls.body: The Capitals are near the top of the league for shots from in close, and the Kraken are near the bottom. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one. Shots from in close tend to be the more dangerous ones.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Kraken take down the Capitals
paras: The first period was a wild one. Kaapo Kakko opened the scoring for the Kraken early in the period, but Jordan Kyrou scored his first goal for Washington midway through the period to tie it 1-1. Alex Ovechkin put the Capitals ahead 2-1 late in the period. Jordan Eberle tied it up for Seattle with 11 seconds left in the first, and Frédérick Gaudreau gave the Kraken the lead late in the second. Boone Jenner tied it 3-3 for Washington just 46 seconds into the third, but that’s where Washington’s luck ran out. Jared McCann and Ryan Winterton scored less than three minutes apart late in the period to put the Kraken up 5-3.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Joey Daccord, who gave up five goals against Vegas in his last start, made 33 saves for the Kraken, and Logan Thompson allowed five goals on 27 shots. By our Swing measure, Adam Larsson had the best night of anyone. The Kraken moved to 4-2-0, and the Capitals fell to 3-2-0.
